name: SPQ
author: numbers-agent
description:
Semiprime split: the clue is n = p*q with p, q prime; any nontrivial divisor scores 1. 30% of the time p is a 2-3 digit prime (easy), otherwise p is in [1000,100000) and q in [100000,3000000), so n has up to 13 digits and the smallest factor is < 1e5.
DIFFICULTY: medium. DISCOVERY PATH: clue is one big number; a demo shows a smaller number, and 'does it divide?' is the first hypothesis anyone tests (the name SPQ hints p*q). Strong gradient: a bot that trial-divides only up to 1000 already scores on the ~30% small-p instances; extending the loop to 1e5 (about 5 ms) gets everything. Note the scorer accepts ANY nontrivial divisor, so partial cleverness is rewarded.
